input.summary:
Master bath furnished in parts/room-15.mjs: west-wall-to-east tub of two water_cauldrons, a cauldron basin by the north window, a dark_oak dressing table with a stool and standing lantern, a barrel dresser, a white carpet rug, and two hanging lanterns. Both doorway lanes are kept clear.
In a scratch build without the lock, light is min 8 with 0 dark cells, FIT is OK, and the layout reads in the picture.
The real build.nbt is written by make.sh, but every furniture write is REFUSED: the shell fills all room interiors with air, so runParts locks those cells. The part is not in the real build yet.
left: REFUSED in the real build: 17 writes (all furniture and lanterns) because parts/shell.mjs line 27 fills the room interior with air, which runParts locks as owned. The fix belongs in the shell: carve only walls and partitions, leave interior cells unwritten. Logged in plan.md Notes.
Walk verdict is UNREACHABLE only because the neighbouring rooms, halls and doors are still stubs in this copy; the walk must be re-run after the other parts land.
Not built: a dressing screen (no clean block read was found in the time), and candles (none placed; light comes from lanterns only).
Checklist not ticked: no elements.md item is actually in the real build yet (the 'Bathrooms x5' item is shared with other rooms).
Scratch harness test-room15.mjs (in this crew dir) runs shell + this room without the lock for checking only; it is not part of make.sh.

waste.what: Discovered the shell's air fill locks every room interior only after the first make.sh run, with a refusal list, so the furniture had to be checked on a separate scratch grid.
waste.cost: one full make.sh run plus a hand-written scratch harness (test-room15.mjs) to test layout without the runParts lock
waste.tool: runParts or the build report could name the owning part for each refused air cell (here: shell line 27) and flag, before parts run, any part whose interior is air-owned by an earlier part.

waste.what: Worked out the 4x7 interior floor grid, lanes and light cells by hand from the plan grid to fill the layers() rows.
waste.cost: several minutes of coordinate reasoning, one re-edit to add the north-east hanging lantern after the light check
waste.tool: $MCD room with a suggested-lamp mode that prints ready layers() rows for the lantern and furniture placements, or a furniture-from-spec helper (room + list of furniture pieces -> layers rows).

waste.what: Walk verdict in a single-room build reads UNREACHABLE because the neighbouring rooms are stubs; no way to tell that apart from a real blocked lane.
waste.cost: one extra check cycle to confirm it was not my lanes
waste.tool: $MCD room could report 'neighbour rooms not built' (doorway leads to air or a stub) separately from a real blocked lane.

companions.task: Fix parts/shell.mjs so the room interiors are not filled with air (carve walls and partitions only), so that room parts can land; I would hand them the refused-write list and the line-27 fill.
Check light once the whole house is built, since the bath's light (min 8 in scratch) depends on the ceiling plate and hanging points staying as the plan says.
